title: OpenAI /v1/chat.completions: streaming handshake, structured annotation envelope, and stop/logprob parity
author: Sofia Patel
description: This PR brings the Redwood OpenAI-compat /v1/chat.completions surface closer to parity by standardizing the streaming handshake, introducing a compact structured 'annotation' envelope for token-level metadata, and normalizing stop/logprob behavior across streaming and non-streaming paths. Motivation: customers have reported mismatches between our streaming frames and OpenAI tooling (incorrect finish_reason, missing per-chunk logprob aggregates, and inconsistent stop enforcement) which complicate downstream tool integrations and evals. Key changes: 1) add a short handshake envelope at stream start ("handshake_v1") that negotiates toolcapabilities and role-hints so client-side tool routing can be deterministic; 2) replace ad-hoc delta fields with a single top-level "annotation" envelope added to stream fragments that can carry stop_mask, logprob_summary, role_hint, and structured_tool_output snippets; 3) enforce stop tokens at both prefix and streaming-fragment boundaries and emit normalized finish_reason values that match OpenAI semantics; 4) compute a per-chunk logprob_summary to avoid leaking huge per-token arrays in the stream while preserving enough info for reranking/eval; 5) add conversion layer for legacy clients via feature flag "compat.v1.streaming_annotations" and deprecation notes for older framed modes. Backwards compatibility and rollout: default remains backward-compatible for existing Redwood clients; the flag is enabled for the Redwood OpenAI-compat gateway and rolled out to 10% of traffic for one week before 100% migration. This PR also updates the Python and TypeScript SDKs to expose the handshake metadata in their streaming iterators. Testing: unit tests for frame serialization, integration test against a local OpenAI-compat harness, and production canary on a subset of customers. Related Linear: ENG-2219 (stream parity), ENG-2278 (stop behavior regression). Checklist: - [x] handshake envelope schema and parser implemented - [x] annotation envelope encoding/decoding in runtime and gateway - [x] SDK exposure for streaming handshake - [x] unit/integration tests - [x] canary rollout plan and monitoring dashboards created - [x] docs updated with migration guide and examples

release_notes: Adds a streaming handshake envelope and a compact structured annotation envelope for token-level metadata (stop_mask, logprob_summary, role_hint, structured_tool_output). Improves stop enforcement and normalizes finish_reason across streaming and non-streaming responses. SDKs updated to surface handshake metadata. Backwards-compatible behind feature flag; rollout via canary.
